question: Despite Minister for Foreign Affairs José Manuel Albares repeatedly stating that Spain has not been selling arms to Israel since 7 October 2023, today it came to light – thanks to research carried out by the Centre Delàs for Peace Studies – that there have been several shipments of weapons and military equipment from Spain to Israel in recent months.

Spain therefore joins the rest of the EU Member States that are continuing to trade arms with Israel despite clear signs suggesting that Israel is committing flagrant war crimes and the fact that the International Court of Justice is investigating Israel for allegedly committing genocide in Gaza.

In light of the Vice-President / High Representative’s recent statements suggesting that there should be a rethink with regard to supplying arms to Israel due to the disproportionate number of people who have been killed in Gaza, and above all considering the obligations and criteria laid down in Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP defining common rules governing control of exports of military technology and equipment: 1.
Does the Vice-President / High Representative believe that the EU should impose a complete embargo on trading arms with Israel?
Does the Vice-President / High Representative plan to formally call on every Member State, including Spain, to immediately suspend all trading of arms and military equipment with Israel?

Joint answer given by High Representative/Vice-President Borrell i Fontelles on behalf of the European Commission (25 June 2024) The control on the export of arms by Member States is subject to national legislation, the Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP (1) and the Arms Trade Treaty (2) (ATT). The competent authorities of Member States take the final decision whether to authorise or deny an individual export or transit license of military equipment, in accordance with the said legal frameworks. |(⸱1|)∙ |(⸱2|)∙

Member States are solely responsible to ensure compliance with applicable laws, including the Common Position and the ATT. The High Representative/Vice-President is not in a position to assess specific export cases against the criteria of the Common Position, nor is mandated, under EU law, to enforce the Common Position or other applicable laws.

The Council, through its competent working group, works towards increased convergence amongst Member States’ arms export policies. This includes exchanges of views on application of criteria of the Common Position.

Specifically, the impact of the conflict in Gaza on national arms exports policies of Member States is continuously on the agenda and Member States confidentially share information about their respective approaches.
